topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture by introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning outcomes on cancer etiology.

topics.label: Intrinsic Chance versus Environmental Influences in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the broad conceptual balance between intrinsic cellular processes and extrinsic exposures in cancer development, supported by public debates and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents contribute to tumorigenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as an illustrative case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis and DNA Damage by Chemical and Physical Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing to form reactive species and cause direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, tumor promoters, and host developmental stages create permissive conditions for malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental, epidemiological, and genomic approaches used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing of the lecture, summarizing key takeaways and highlighting personal and societal risk-benefit assessments.
